done_when: The hand-back reverts only the worker's own forge.toml edits, keeps settings that came from merging the default branch, and a test with a round that merges main's changed settings keeps them, on new and adopted repos

known.title: Preserve inherited settings on stacked fixes

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Functional. The merge-base comparison treats settings inherited before the round as this worker's edits. `src/forge/task.py:520–530` explicitly starts a child fix from an unmerged parent's HEAD. If the parent legitimately changes forge.toml and the child fixes unrelated product code, settings_allowed is false for the child. Its hand-back now commits a restoration that discards the parent's settings, such as a required test command, even when the child worker never touched forge.toml. Preserve the round's inherited settings while accounting for incoming default-branch changes.
findings.title: Preserve inherited settings on stacked fixes

why: When a build round merges main after main's forge.toml changed, the hand-back treats main's new settings as the worker's edit and restores the round's old copy, so merging the fix reverts main's settings
